title: Paint House
summary: Given a row of n houses, each needing to be painted one of three colors (red, blue, or green) with different costs, find the minimum total cost to paint all houses ensuring no two adjacent houses share the same color.
statement: Given a row of n houses, each needing to be painted one of three colors (red, blue, or green) with different costs, find the minimum total cost to paint all houses ensuring no two adjacent houses share the same color. The cost for each house and color is provided in a cost matrix.
constraints: costs has 1–100 rows and exactly three integer costs from 1 to 20 per row.
Choose one color per house so adjacent houses differ. Return the minimum total cost; the three columns consistently represent the same three colors.
hints: The best cost ending in a color depends on the two different colors from the previous house.
Keep three running costs, one for each possible last color.
For each new row, add its red cost to min(previous blue,green), and analogously for the other colors.
Use the previous three values together when computing the next row; in-place sequential updates would mix stages.
editorial: The state for each color is the cheapest valid painting of the processed prefix ending in that color. Appending a house may use either of the other two prior states, giving the three transitions. Only one previous row is required. The independent oracle enumerates every color assignment for small seeded inputs and rejects adjacent equal colors.

tests.explanation: Choose color columns 1,2,1 for costs 2+5+3=10; adjacent colors differ.
With one house there is no adjacency restriction, so choose its minimum cost 2.
